headers.comment: The panel is a single HTML file, so a cached copy means the operator keeps using an OLD admin panel after a fix ships — which is exactly what happened with the update-form guard: it was deployed and live, but the browser kept serving the previous page and let a bad value through anyway. NOTE the source list: Hosting matches headers on the REQUEST PATH, and the panel is opened as `/`, which `**/*.html` does NOT match — that miss is why the first attempt at this changed nothing.

The APK is what the in-app updater downloads, and Hosting's default for a static asset is max-age=3600. So for an HOUR after a deploy the CDN can hand out the PREVIOUS build while the panel already advertises the new versionCode - the user installs what they already have, the app still sees an update, and that is an update LOOP with no bad version number anywhere. Caught 2026-09-07 by the download-back check: the panel URL returned vC 130 minutes after vC 132 was deployed, and only a cache-busting query string produced the real file. `no-cache` and NOT `no-store`: revalidation is what is needed, and a 304 on an unchanged 16MB binary is worth keeping. Both forms are listed for the reason recorded above - Hosting matches on the REQUEST PATH.
